messages:
Jordan (support): :rotating_light: Acme reports huge spike in 5xx/timeouts hitting Redwood hosted API since this morning's canary. ~25% of requests failing. @tom_oncall can you triage?  

Tom (oncall): On it. Any customer repro or sample request/ids?  

Jordan (support): They sent a failing curl and a request id: req_98765. cURL returns 502 with body "gateway timeout". short sample: 

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
> {
>   "error": "upstream timeout"
> }
```

Tom (oncall): Thanks. I'm checking canary rollout logs. DeployBot, show canary metadata for rollout id 5678.

DeployBot: Canary rollout 5678 -> model-server-v3.14, config profile=low-latency, flags: prefetch=true, batching_window_ms=0, kvcache_enabled=true. Started 2025-10-03T09:12:00Z

Lee (runtime): Whoa batching_window_ms=0 looks wrong. That effectively disables batching control and triggers immediate path that overwhelms proxies. I see connection resets and queued requests in the canary pool.

Priya (sre): Confirming spikes on gateway: 5xx rate jumped from 0.6% -> 24% at rollout start. Latency p50 p95 both increased. Traces show repeated upstream timeouts to runtime nodes.

Lee (runtime): Also noticed the canary env had an older kernel selection; apparently v3.14 picked fallback kernels due to quantization mismatch. Combined with batching=0 it amplifies per-token CPU, dropping capacity.

Tom (oncall): Can we roll the canary back to v3.13 while we debug? Need coordination with product for rollback window.

Jordan (support): Acme notified that we're investigating and will roll back if needed. They've started collecting traffic ids. :+1:

Priya (sre): Proposed rollback command:

```
ORCH> orchestrator rollback --rollout=5678 --target-version=v3.13 --type=canary
```

Tom (oncall): Executing rollback now. DeployBot, initiate rollback 5678 -> v3.13.

DeployBot: Rollback started for rollout 5678. Target version v3.13. Progress: 20% -> 50% -> 100%

Lee (runtime): After rollback, backend error rate dropping. I'm seeing per-node load return to baseline. Also set a temporary guard to reject canaries with batching_window_ms <= 1.

Tom (oncall): Patching config validation to block batching_window_ms=0 for future rollouts. Creating PR.

Jordan (support): Updated Acme: rollback complete, we're continuing to monitor. They appreciate the quick response.

Priya (sre): Current metrics: 5xx down to 0.8%, latency back to expected. I'll keep monitoring for 30m.

Tom (oncall): Root cause summary for postmortem: misconfigured canary flag (batching_window_ms=0) + kernel fallback on v3.14 => overload -> upstream timeouts and gateway 5xx. Remediation: rollback, config validation, guard in release pipeline, add automated canary health check for 5xx spike >5%.

Jordan (support): Filing support follow-up and customer RCA with Acme. Closing incident when monitoring window ends. :white_check_mark:

Acme_integration: Thanks team, service looks normal from our side. Appreciate the quick rollback.
